name: David C. Plummer
why_notable: Author of RFC 826 (November 1982), 'An Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol', now Internet Standard STD 37. Written as the DEC/Intel/Xerox 10 Mbit Ethernet spread, it solved a basic gap: protocol addresses (32-bit DoD Internet, 16-bit CHAOS, 8-bit Xerox PUP) had no relation to 48-bit Ethernet hardware addresses. His answer, a broadcast request and a direct reply cached by both sides, was deliberately protocol-generic and is still how every IPv4 host on a LAN finds its neighbours over 40 years later. The same design has no authentication, which is why ARP spoofing works and why tools like arp-scan can find every host on a segment. Later updated by RFC 5227 (conflict detection) and replaced in IPv6 by Neighbor Discovery.
